_meta.confidence_note: Every fact below is tagged 'confidence: primary_confirmed' (found verbatim in the OCR'd or clean-text primary Act) or 'confidence: secondary_corroborated' (agreed upon by 2+ independent reputable secondary sources — EY, Baker Tilly, Aluko & Oyebode, KPMG, Mercans/Safeguard Global — but not yet grep-confirmed in the primary text, usually because OCR phrasing/spacing didn't match a search pattern). small_company_rate.cite: NTA s.56/57 area: 'a small company, at 0%'

standard_company_rate.cite: NTA: 'any other company, at the rate of 30% from the commencement of this Act'

large_multinational_minimum_effective_ta.cite: EY / Baker Tilly summaries of NTA effective tax rate provisions for large/multinational groups

turnover_threshold.value: NGN 100,000,000 (₦100 million) annual gross turnover or below
turnover_threshold.note: raised from the prior ₦25 million threshold under the old CIT Act
turnover_threshold.cite: EY / Baker Tilly / Aluko & Oyebode summaries

fixed_assets_threshold.value: NGN 250,000,000 (₦250 million) total fixed assets or below

small_company_definition.note: A company meeting BOTH thresholds is 'small' and is exempt from CIT, Capital Gains Tax, and the Development Levy.

standard_rate.note: unchanged from the pre-reform rate; multiple independent sources confirm no change
standard_rate.cite: EY, Baker Tilly, Kuda Business summaries

input_vat_credit.value: Businesses can now claim input VAT credit on most purchases (previously restricted to goods for resale/production)

small_company_exemption.value: Small companies (as defined above) are exempt from deducting WHT at source where the transaction value is NGN 2,000,000 (₦2 million) or less AND the supplier has a valid Tax Identification Number (TIN)

deemed_distribution_rate.note: applies to undistributed profits of a closely-held Nigerian company controlled by 5 or fewer individuals, deemed distributed and subject to WHT at 10%

companies_rate.note: raised from the prior flat 10% CGT rate for companies; companies' capital gains are now effectively taxed at the standard CIT rate

individuals.value: Capital gains for individuals are now taxed under the personal income tax bands (up to 25%), replacing the prior flat 10% CGT rate

small_company_exemption.value: Small companies (as defined above) are exempt from CGT

exempt_threshold.value: Individuals earning below NGN 800,000 (₦800,000) per annum are exempt from PIT

rent_relief.value: 20% of annual rent paid, capped at a maximum of NGN 500,000 (₦500,000), replacing the previous Consolidated Relief Allowance
rent_relief.note: requires the individual to declare annual rent and provide supporting information to the tax authority

rate.cite: NTA s.59(1): 'A development levy of 4% is imposed on the assessable profits ... of all companies chargeable to tax'

base.value: Assessable profits of companies chargeable to tax under Chapters Two and Three of the Act

exemptions.value: Small companies and non-resident companies are exempt from the Development Levy
exemptions.cite: NTA s.59 area: 'other than small companies and non-resident companies'

replaces.value: Consolidates and replaces the former Tertiary Education Tax, Nigeria Police Trust Fund levy, and other earmarked taxes into one unified levy

rule.value: An individual is a Nigerian tax resident if physically present in Nigeria for 183 days or more within any 12-month period

non_resident_taxation.value: Non-residents are taxed only on Nigerian-source income (e.g. rental income from Nigerian property, dividends from Nigerian companies, profits from Nigerian business operations)

resident_taxation.value: Residents may be taxed on worldwide income, subject to applicable reliefs, allowances, and exemptions

foreign_earned_income_exemption.value: Income earned entirely outside Nigeria by a non-resident (including remote work for foreign employers) is exempt from Nigerian tax even if remitted into Nigeria

remittances_not_taxable.value: Genuine personal remittances (family support, gifts, community contributions, personal transfers) are NOT taxable income

double_taxation_relief.value: Nigeria has Double Taxation Agreements (DTAs) with several countries (e.g. UK, Canada, South Africa); where no DTA exists, the Act provides unilateral relief to prevent double taxation

who_needs_a_tin.value: Required only for individuals or entities with taxable income or business activities in Nigeria

individual_tin_via_nin.value: Individuals may obtain a TIN using their National Identification Number (NIN)

company_tin.value: Companies receive a TIN automatically upon registration with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC)

existing_business_without_tin.value: May apply through the Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) / Nigeria Revenue Service

ngos.value: Remain tax-exempt provided they are properly registered, operate for charitable purposes, and comply with reporting requirements

smes.value: Taxed like other Nigerian businesses but eligible for the small-company exemptions and sector-specific incentives described above

authority.name: Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) — being reconstituted as the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) under the Nigeria Revenue Service (Establishment) Act, 2025

annual_returns_deadline.value: A company in business more than 18 months: file within 6 months after the end of its accounting year. A newly incorporated company: within 18 months of incorporation, or 6 months after the end of its first accounting period, whichever is earlier. A company permanently ceasing trade: within 6 months of ceasing.
annual_returns_deadline.cite: Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, s. on time of filing returns

penalty_failure_to_register.value: NGN 50,000 for the first month of failing/refusing to register for tax, then NGN 25,000 for each subsequent month the failure continues. A statutory body or company that awards a contract to an unregistered person is also liable to a penalty.
penalty_failure_to_register.cite: Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, s.100(1)-(2) (Failure to register)
